SemIf
Semantic ifs, read from a server-side diffusion model.

A live, local experiment

Decision model on your server.

A server-side DiffusionGemma reads a probability for each of your allowed options in a single denoising pass, and returns the distribution — no token-by-token decoding, no WebGPU, no weights leaving the machine it runs on. Type a decision and measure the read.

03 / server timing

Where the time goes

synchronized

Prefill and decode are measured on the server with synchronized timers, then reported per question. This lane is honest accounting, not a second method.

Timings are measured with performance.now() around the HTTP round-trip on this page. Server-side prefill/decode are reported separately above. Sequential questions; no parallel execution is claimed.

What these numbers do—and do not—mean

Conditional probabilities. The returned distribution is normalized across your options only. It is not calibrated confidence and does not cover every answer the model might prefer.

Confidence is a local approximation. The header X-Arcaine-Confidence-Method: normalized-entropy-v1 marks it: 1 − H(p)/log K on the averaged distribution. It is not Jev's confidence formula.

One pass per read. Each read is a single denoising pass over a compiled answer canvas; repeated reads average fresh-noise samples. Question IDs never enter inference.

Not Jev. The format is Jev-compatible; the weights and internal scoring are Arcaine's DiffusionGemma backend. Hosted Jev quality and latency are not claimed.
